items.prompt: Define financial rewards. [2]
items.canonical_answer: Financial rewards are money payments received for work, including basic pay and cash incentives. They can meet living costs and provide a clear performance reward. Their effect depends on amount, fairness, reliability and what the employee values. A cash allowance remains a money reward even when intended to cover travel or housing. It differs from supplying the service itself.
marking_guidance: Meaning: Financial rewards are money payments received for work, including basic pay and cash incentives.

items.prompt: Define non-financial rewards. [2]
items.canonical_answer: Non-financial rewards provide benefits other than direct cash payments, such as recognition, achievement, meaningful responsibility, development or an employer-provided service. They may improve satisfaction and retention, but their relevance depends on staff needs and design. They can cost the employer money and do not remove its obligation to pay agreed wages. A cash bonus is financial even if labelled an appreciation benefit.

items.prompt: Explain how reward design can affect Eno’s effort and quality. Fictional Eno Packs rewards the number of packs made, while customers complain about poorly sealed packs. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Rewards can influence willingness to work, effort, retention and satisfaction when staff value them and see a credible link between performance and reward. A reward seen as unfair, unattainable or unrelated to a person’s contribution may fail to motivate. Match the arrangement to the task and needs: individual output pay can encourage measurable work, while team recognition can support cooperation. A narrowly defined target can also divert effort from quality or service. Financial incentives do not replace acceptable conditions or solve every problem of monotonous work. Non-financial responsibility needs genuine authority and support, not simply extra duties with blame attached. Review both staff responses and business outcomes rather than assuming a higher payment automatically improves everything. The reward can encourage speed but neglects the customer’s quality requirement. Paying for acceptable packs and monitoring quality would align the incentive better, while worker consultation can reveal practical obstacles.
marking_guidance: Starting point: Rewards can influence willingness to work, effort, retention and satisfaction when staff value them and see a credible link between performance and reward.

items.prompt: Explain how basic pay plus an incentive differs from a pure output-payment system. Fictional Tuli Sales pays a basic amount plus a percentage of sales value. Fictional Oka Assembly pays for hours worked with a bonus for meeting an agreed quality-and-output target. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Payment systems include salary, wages based on time or output, combination systems, bonuses, fringe benefits, commissions, productivity agreements and profit sharing. A salary commonly fixes an annual amount paid in regular instalments. Time work pays for time worked; piece work pays for acceptable units; a combination mixes a basic payment with an incentive. Bonuses are additional rewards against stated conditions. Commission links earnings to sales, while profit sharing distributes an agreed portion of profit. A productivity agreement links a negotiated improvement in output per input with rewards. Fringe benefits supply non-cash benefits. Some arrangements overlap: a salesperson can have a salary plus commission and an employer-provided service. State the base and the incentive separately, including the outcome each rewards. The first is salary or basic pay plus commission; the second combines time work with a conditional bonus. Neither should be described as pure piece work, since neither pays solely per acceptable unit.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Payment systems include salary, wages based on time or output, combination systems, bonuses, fringe benefits, commissions, productivity agreements and profit sharing.

A busy month does not by itself change that contractual base.

A different weekly worker could instead be paid per acceptable item.

items.canonical_answer: A productivity agreement is a negotiated arrangement linking improved output per input to an agreed reward or benefit. The agreement links reward to efficiency, not merely a larger total order. Jointly checking labour hours and acceptable output helps determine whether the stated condition is met.

items.prompt: Explain how Hena’s work organisation can give staff meaningful responsibility. Fictional Hena Repairs lets competent technicians choose routine repair methods within agreed safety and spending limits, rather than seek approval for each step. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Work organisation can give staff meaningful responsibility through delegation, team decisions and job enrichment, or remove discretion by centralising decisions and narrowing tasks. Responsibility should be matched with authority and resources. A wide span of control may leave subordinates more independent if managers delegate appropriately, but a headcount alone does not prove they have authority. A narrow span can support close supervision and development but can also become restrictive if every routine decision needs approval. Staff differ in readiness and desire for responsibility. Give support and clear boundaries, then review outcomes instead of equating less supervision with abandonment. Job enlargement adds tasks at a similar level; enrichment adds meaningful responsibility or challenge, so more repetitive duties alone need not motivate. Genuine discretion can provide achievement and faster service. The owner retains oversight and must check competence; merely assigning more jobs without decision rights would not create the same responsibility.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Work organisation can give staff meaningful responsibility through delegation, team decisions and job enrichment, or remove discretion by centralising decisions and narrowing tasks.

It compares pure piece work with basic time pay plus a quality-and-output bonus. Staff value stable earnings. items.canonical_answer: a Pure piece work fits measurable identical units but exposes income to the item count and may reward rushing unless acceptance standards are clear. Choose the combination for income stability and quality, with attainable targets and fair assessment. b Unique repairs remove comparable unit counts: a worker handling a difficult repair could appear less productive than one receiving easy work. Pure piece work becomes less suitable, and the original quantity-based bonus also needs redesign. Retain basic time pay and use carefully assessed quality, customer-service or team outcomes if a bonus is feasible. The preference for a stable base holds, but the bonus measure must change because counting finished items no longer represents comparable performance.
